key_concepts: Work is done when a force causes displacement of an object
Work requires both an applied force and a resulting displacement
Work is calculated using W = F d cos(θ)
Work is maximum when force and displacement are parallel
Work is zero when force and displacement are perpendicular
Negative work occurs when force and displacement are opposite
Power is the rate of doing work or transferring energy
Power is calculated using P = W/t
Power can also be calculated as P = F v cos(θ)
High power means the same work is done in less time
Work is measured in joules or ergs; power in watts
Kilowatt-hour is a unit of electric energy equal to 1000 watts for one hour
